simple: A long project that joins several things you built before into one system.
analogy: A whole house built by several trades.
precise: In this university, one of the eight capstones MP1–MP8: one to two semesters, alone or in a small team, with milestones, deliverables, a grading rubric and the review gates R0–R4; each reuses curriculum milestones as building blocks and adds integration, scale and real-world constraints.
source: D1 of F12-28: University Authoring Guide section 11.6 (this project's own rules, opened in this build)

simple: A step whose test only passes when two or more parts work together.
analogy: The day the kitchen wall is closed over pipes and cables.
precise: An MP8 milestone defined by the learner and approved at R1, whose acceptance test exercises a path crossing at least one interface contract between components (course definition).
source: D1 of F12-28: guide section 11.6, MP8 card (course definition built on it)

simple: A written agreement about exactly what passes between two parts.
analogy: The drawing of where each pipe crosses the wall, and how wide it is.
precise: A versioned specification of the messages or calls between two components: names, types, units, ranges, ordering, error and timeout behaviour, and the rule for unknown fields; part of the design document and owned by both sides (course definition).
source: F12-28 course definition, extending the design-document sections of F12-02 (pending verification against a tier 3 source)

simple: A test that checks one side keeps the agreement, without the other side running.
analogy: Checking the hole in the wall with the agreed pipe size before the plumber arrives.
precise: An automated test that feeds a component inputs, or reads its outputs, exactly as the interface contract specifies, including its named edge cases, so that both components can be tested separately and integration failures become contract violations with an owner (course definition).
source: F12-28 course definition; no source opened in this build (unverified box in F12-28 Layer 2)

simple: The thinnest version of the whole system that works from end to end.
analogy: One finished room with water, power and a door, before the others.
precise: An early milestone in which every component exists, real or stubbed behind its contract, and one representative request travels the complete path, checked by an automated end-to-end test; later milestones replace stubs without changing the path (course definition).
source: F12-28 course definition; no source opened in this build (unverified box in F12-28 Layer 2)

simple: Work that is really happening but is not in the plan.
analogy: Moving a pipe that nobody wrote on the job list.
precise: Effort spent on a task that has no milestone, estimate or acceptance test in the plan, usually discovered as time a planned milestone spent blocked; it makes the critical path and forecasts wrong (course definition; detected by F12-28 Listing 1).
source: F12-28 course definition and R1 (lab run of Listing 1 in this build)

simple: A new estimate of the end date, made from how the project has really gone so far.
analogy: After three rooms took longer than planned, you expect the next rooms to take longer too.
precise: In F12-28 Listing 1, a forward pass over the dependency graph in which finished milestones take their actual durations and unfinished ones their likely estimate times the observed ratio of actual to likely; a simple model with stated assumptions, not a validated prediction method.
source: F12-28 course definition and R1 (lab run of Listing 1 in this build); accuracy unverified (unverified box in F12-28 Layer 3)

simple: A planned stop where other people check the project before it goes on.
analogy: The building inspector's visit at a fixed stage.
precise: In this university's mega projects, one of the reviews R0 (proposal), R1 (design review), R2 (mid-project review), R3 (readiness review) and R4 (final defence); a gate is passed only with written reviewer approval by peer learners and, where available, a human mentor; agent reviewers may assist; the owner decides who signs.
source: D1 of F12-29: University Authoring Guide section 11.6 (this project's own rules, opened in this build)

simple: The list of things that must be ready before a review can start.
analogy: The walls must still be open for the wiring inspection.
precise: A list of evidence items and acceptance tests, written and approved at the previous gate, that must be present and passing for a gate to be held; fixing them in advance keeps the evidence from being chosen after the result is known (course definition).
source: F12-29 course definition

simple: Everything the reviewers need, sent before the meeting.
analogy: The drawings and the open walls, ready when the inspector arrives.
precise: The gate record, the documents under review, and the logs and test outputs named as evidence, as files the reviewers can open or commands they can rerun, sent ahead of the meeting (course definition).
source: F12-29 course definition

simple: The result of a review: yes, yes-if, or not yet.
analogy: 'Move in', 'move in, railing fixed by Friday', 'call me when the alarm works'.
precise: One of PASS (all entry criteria met, independent approvals present), PASS WITH CONDITIONS (as PASS, with recorded conditions that do not touch safety items) or NOT YET (at least one blocking finding; the gate is held again after the fix); course definition implemented by F12-29 Listing 1.
source: F12-29 course definition and R1 (lab run of Listing 1 in this build)

simple: A small thing that must be done after a pass, by a named person, by a date.
analogy: The loose stair railing.
precise: A recorded requirement attached to a PASS WITH CONDITIONS outcome, with an owner, a due date and the evidence that will close it; it may not defer an entry criterion marked as safety (course definition).
source: F12-29 course definition

simple: A reviewer who did not do the work.
analogy: The inspector is not the builder.
precise: A reviewer who is not an author of the work under review; the guide applies the same principle to its own pipeline, where author, fact-checker and editor are distinct runs and an agent never marks its own work as checked.
source: D1 of F12-29: University Authoring Guide sections 3.7 (AH-36) and 12.2 (opened in this build)

simple: The check just before the risky part.
analogy: The inspection before anyone moves in.
precise: Gate R3 of the mega projects; for MP6 and MP7 the safety and go/no-go review before any real robot run or flight, with a fixed list of physical checks; for MP8 held before the game-day and before any real-hardware run.
source: D1 of F12-29: University Authoring Guide section 11.6 (opened in this build)

simple: The last review, where you show your project and answer questions in public.
analogy: The walk-through when the house is handed over.
precise: Gate R4 of MP8 and the exam of SE501: a public, oral defence with a demonstration, graded with the MP8 rubric (technical depth 25 %, integration quality 20 %, evidence and testing 20 %, leadership and communication 20 %, reflection 15 %).
source: D1 of F12-30: University Authoring Guide sections 5.17 and 11.6 (opened in this build)

simple: The exact list of steps you will show, written in advance, that checks itself.
analogy: The walk-through route, stop by stop.
precise: A versioned, deterministic input (scenario, configuration, fault injections) that drives the system from a clean build through the behaviour being defended and prints machine-checkable acceptance results (course definition).
source: F12-30 course definition; R1 (lab run of Listing 1 in this build)

simple: A saved earlier run of the same demonstration, used if the live one cannot run.
analogy: The folder of inspection records.
precise: The output and run record (toolchain, command, date, machine, exit code) of the demonstration script from a clean build, made before the defence and labelled as a recording, never presented as live (course definition, following the curriculum's rule that recorded hardware runs are extra evidence, never a replacement).
source: F12-30 course definition; D2 of F12-30: Systems Curriculum section 0 (opened in this build)

simple: A list of everything you will claim, each with the evidence that backs it.
analogy: The list of promises to the buyers, each with its certificate.
precise: A table of a defence's claims, each typed as a claim or a limitation and linked to evidence items (test logs with results, measurements with machine, date and run count, sources with whether they were opened); F12-30 Listing 2 rejects claims without usable evidence (course definition applying the guide's claim tagging, AH-15).
source: F12-30 course definition; D1 of F12-30: University Authoring Guide section 3.3

simple: Something you say your system does not do, or was not tested for.
analogy: 'The attic is not insulated yet.'
precise: A claim about the boundary of the evidence (untested conditions, cut scope, known faults and their status), stated by the author so that no listener extends a claim beyond what was shown (course definition).
source: F12-30 course definition

simple: A save that the system has told you is done.
analogy: The builder says the pipe is connected, and you close the wall.
precise: In the F12-30 worked example's store, a write for which the ground station received ACK; the store's interface contract must state on how many replicas an acknowledged write is stored, and acceptance check A1 requires every acknowledged write to be readable after failover. The store is the university's teaching model, not a real product or the Raft algorithm.
source: F12-30 course definition; R1–R3 (lab runs of Listing 1 in this build)

simple: Looking back at the whole project to decide what you would do differently next time.
analogy: After handing over the house, the team asks what they would change on the next one.
precise: An MP8 deliverable: a written reflection on what the learner would do differently, built in SE501 from records (plan against actual, gate findings, incidents) rather than memory; graded under reflection (15 %).
source: D1 of F12-30: University Authoring Guide section 11.6 (opened in this build)
